title_en: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
title_zh: 被困俄罗斯占领城市多年的乌克兰撤离人员与家人团聚
summary: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
summary_zh: 奥列什基居民一直没有食物、水和电，许多人靠烹饪花园里的杂草来生存。
body_en: By Dan Johnson , Ukraine correspondent , Reporting from Chernihiv and Jacob Phillips
There were raw emotional scenes as people evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed from Belarus into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv.
Families cried as they reunited with relatives they had not seen for years, with two sisters running and crying out as they embraced their father.

Some elderly residents were so weak they were carried on stretchers. They had been trapped in the frontline city without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for her efforts in brokering a local ceasefire that paved the way for their evacuation on Friday.
Upon their arrival, Dasha and Anya Palii sprinted across the tarmac screaming towards the bus carrying their father Mykhailo.
Their cries and their tears captured the sheer relief of three years of desperate worry, fearing they would never see him again.
Their mother Zhanna clasped Mykhailo's face and stroked his forehead again and again, as if checking he was the same man she had left behind. He promised her, finally, they will now get married.

Tetiana and Volodymyr, an older couple carrying their cat, told the BBC they no longer have a home, after it was burned down in the first year of the war. They have been living in the abandoned house of a neighbour.
They said they instantly took the decision to leave but feared their journey could be disrupted. Now they have to work out where to go next and how to rebuild their lives.

Ukrainian military positions lie just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees first had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border on Saturday.
The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

Zelensky said in a post on X that "all of them will receive the assistance they need. It is important that government agencies and all the regional and local authorities involved work effectively and help our people adapt."

Many people bear the scars: the convoy includes as many ambulances as coaches. The impact of years caught between the frontlines is written on the weary faces of many of Oleshky's residents, some hobbling on crutches, others needing wheelchairs.
They have a lot to come to terms with, not least having left the place they call home.

A humanitarian ceasefire took effect across the frontline region of Kherson on Tuesday, providing the first few days of peace in the area in four years, following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Before the war, Oleshky was home to 24,000 people.

Conditions had become so desperate in the city that not only was getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape was highly dangerous because the routes out had been mined and subject to drone attack.
Bridges across the nearby River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank has been mined and is dangerous.
One resident who fled the city three weeks earlier told the BBC he had walked through 24km (15 miles) of minefields to get to safety.
The ceasefire allowed the road out of the city to be cleared of mines and humanitarian aid to be delivered.
body_zh: 丹·约翰逊，乌克兰记者，切尔尼戈夫和雅各布·菲利普斯报道
当人们从被俄罗斯占领的奥列什基市撤离，从白俄罗斯越境进入乌克兰切尔尼戈夫地区时，出现了令人激动的场景。
当家人与多年未见的亲戚团聚时，他们哭了，两个姐妹一边跑一边哭着拥抱父亲。
一些老人身体虚弱，只能用担架抬走。他们被困在前线城市，没有食物、水和电，许多人靠烹饪花园里的杂草来生存。
乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基感谢美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普为促成当地停火所做的努力，为周五的撤离铺平了道路。
抵达后，达莎和安雅·帕利冲过停机坪，尖叫着冲向载着父亲米凯洛的巴士。
他们的哭声和泪水让三年来的绝望忧虑得到了彻底的缓解，担心他们再也见不到他了。
他们的母亲詹娜捧着米凯洛的脸，一次又一次地抚摸他的额头，仿佛要确认他还是她留下的那个人。他最终向她保证，他们现在就要结婚。
Tetiana 和 Volodymyr 是一对带着猫的老夫妇，他们告诉 BBC，自从战争第一年被烧毁后，他们就不再有家了。他们一直住在邻居废弃的房子里。
他们说，他们立即决定离开，但担心他们的旅程可能会受到干扰。现在他们必须弄清楚下一步该去哪里以及如何重建他们的生活。
乌克兰军事阵地距离奥列什基仅 5 公里（3.1 英里），但撤离人员首先必须穿过俄罗斯占领的领土前往俄罗斯南部，然后飞往白俄罗斯，最后于周六被驱车穿过乌克兰北部边境。
乌克兰人权监察员德米特罗·鲁比涅茨 (Dmytro Lubinets) 表示，撤离者中年龄最大的是 94 岁，最年轻的只有 1 岁。
泽连斯基在 X 上发帖称，“他们所有人都将获得所需的援助。重要的是，政府机构以及所有相关地区和地方当局必须有效工作并帮助我们的人民适应。”
许多人都留下了伤疤：车队中的救护车和教练一样多。奥列什基的许多居民疲惫的脸上都写满了多年来在前线的影响，有些人拄着拐杖一瘸一拐，另一些人则需要轮椅。
他们有很多事情要面对，尤其是离开了他们称之为家的地方。
周二，人道主义停火在赫尔松前线地区生效，这是该地区自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来四年来首次实现和平。战前，奥列什基居住着 24,000 人。
这座城市的情况已经变得非常严峻，不仅将物资运送到城市极其困难，而且逃跑也非常危险，因为出去的路线布满了地雷，并且容易受到无人机的袭击。
附近第聂伯河上的桥梁已被摧毁，消息人士称河岸已布有地雷，十分危险。
一名三周前逃离该市的居民告诉 BBC，他穿过 24 公里（15 英里）的雷区才到达安全地带。
停火使得出城道路上的地雷得以清除，人道主义援助得以运送。

title_en: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent
title_zh: 德国生活成本抗议演变成暴力，商店被洗劫
summary: Police in Frankfurt say "violent riots" took place in the city centre, with unrest also reported in Berlin, Hamburg and Cologne.
summary_zh: 法兰克福警方表示，市中心发生了“暴力骚乱”，柏林、汉堡和科隆也有报道称发生骚乱。
body_en: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent - BBC News
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday and clashes erupted with police there and in other German cities after largely peaceful mass protests over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who targeted emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands earlier joined the demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.
The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.
A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police, AFP news agency reported. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.
Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website.
Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".
She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."
Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?
While protests during the day were largely peaceful, the demonstrations turned violent as night fell.

In a post on X, Frankfurt police said that "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.
In later updates, officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect.

Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the capital, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.

Poseck said: "We all have those images from France in our minds – looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."

body_zh: 德国生活成本抗议演变成暴力，商店被洗劫 -_澳门赌博平台
周六晚间，暴乱者抢劫了法兰克福市中心的商店，并在针对生活成本的大规模和平抗议活动之后，当地和德国其他城市与警方爆发了冲突。
除了德国金融中心法兰克福外，柏林、科隆和汉堡也发生了暴力事件，警方表示，他们使用高压水枪驱散抗议者，这些抗议者向急救人员投掷烟花、石块和瓶子。
早些时候，数千人参加了运动团体 Gen Z regelt（意思是“Z 世代负责”）组织的示威活动，抗议学校资金不足、生活成本高昂、公共开支削减和兵役。
德国发生骚乱之前，法国也发生了类似的青年领导的大规模抗议活动，周六也有超过 32 万人示威。
据法新社报道，法兰克福主要购物街的一大片区域已被警方封锁。警方发言人表示，该市逮捕了许多人。
法兰克福、慕尼黑和柏林当局报告称抗议者人数多达 18,000 人，大约是组织者在其网站上估计人数的一半。
Gen Z regelt 发言人莉娜·弗里德里希 (Lina Friedrich) 表示，示威活动是“为了和平与自由而战，而不是为了战争和胁迫”。
她说：“对我们来说最重要的是更好地支持卫生和教育系统。我们反对义务兵役制，我们赞成更公平地分配负担。”
欧洲的年轻人正在前进——但有什么东西能够真正将他们团结起来呢？
虽然白天的抗议活动基本上是和平的，但随着夜幕降临，示威活动变得暴力。
法兰克福警方在 X 上发帖称，市中心正在发生“暴力骚乱”。警方称，几家商店的窗户被砸碎，并向紧急服务部门投掷燃烧弹。
在后来的更新中，官员们表示，一家枪店的窗户被砸碎，他们在逮捕一名嫌疑人后缴获了两件武器。
法兰克福为首府的黑森州内政部长罗曼·波塞克(Roman Poseck)表示，“大约100名明确身份的左翼极端分子”已渗透到该市的抗议活动中。他补充说，抗议活动的结束方式是“可耻的”。
波塞克说：“我们脑海中都有来自法国的那些画面——抢劫、焚烧房屋、焚烧警车、袭击警察……法国在这方面绝不能成为榜样。”

title_en: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
title_zh: 塞尔维亚总统武契奇的垮台如何反映了匈牙利奥尔班的垮台
summary: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.
summary_zh: 塞尔维亚的亚历山大·武契奇(Aleksandar Vučiċ)在上周末的投票中落败，是维克多·欧尔班(Viktor Orbán)在匈牙利倒台的翻版。
body_en: When they met in northern Serbia last November, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučiċ and Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán could hardly have guessed they would both be out of power within a year.

Both were ousted by popular movements - Orbán fell first, in April, defeated by Péter Magyar's Tisza party. Then last Sunday a student movement less than two years old won Serbia's parliamentary elections by a landslide.

The Tisza party in Hungary and the Student List in Serbia look very different - Tisza is centred on the personality and energy of its leader, while the students in Serbia insist they have no leadership.

But the huge turnout - 79% in Hungary and 69% in Serbia, was driven by tech-savvy young people in both countries. They used AI tools to crunch numbers, identify threats to the vote, and mobilise tens of thousands of election monitors to prevent intimidation and electoral fraud by the governing parties.
Mobilisation of voters, and the role of election monitors, played a big role in the opposition victory in both countries.

Last weekend, the DE civic action group in Hungary sent 70 election monitors to Serbia, to work with students' movement representatives, visiting polling stations in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina.
During the summer, even before the election was called, they held workshops to share their experience and methods from the Hungarian election with the Serbian students.

A key technique was to identify "infected" polling districts in advance - places where the surprisingly high number of votes for the governing party at previous elections suggested that voter intimidation or "chain voting" techniques were used.

"From around 16:00 on election day, we noticed groups of masked hooligans - Vučiċ supporters - gathering near voting stations," Péter Klemm, a student activist from Subotica, told the BBC. "So we sent mobile teams, and started filming everything."
Combined with the "stationary" monitors already in place, 20 to 30 volunteers at each threatened polling station acted as a strong deterrent, he believes, and prevented intimidation or fraud.

Orbán in Hungary, Vučiċ in Serbia, both looked invincible. Both were powerful leaders, in office for 16 and 14 years, who had taken over state institutions and established business empires overlapping the two countries.
Orban chose cheese, Vučiċ meat, when they sat down to a quick lunch of traditional burek pastries at a small, popular town centre bakery in Subotica almost a year ago.

They continued to a local winery, to talk about oil and other business deals - the planned Hungarian purchase of Serbia's Nis oil refinery. The two nationalist leaders found much in common, in business and politics, not least their friendship with Vladimir Putin in Russia and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and their strong support for Milorad Dodik, the separatist leader of the Bosnian Serbs.
A high-speed railway between Belgrade and Budapest is being built with Chinese finance and know-how.

The parallels between the fall from power of the two men are extraordinary. Aleksandar Vučiċ admitted defeat at exactly 21:30 on Sunday evening, just as Viktor Orbán did on 12 April. Few observers expected either leader to concede peacefully.

There has been speculation this week that Vučiċ spoke to Orbán twice on Sunday night to ask his advice - once before he conceded, and again at 23:15. And that Orbán convinced his Serbian ally not to use force.
Vučiċ denies that he spoke to Orbán before he made his announcement, but acknowledges the later conversation. Viktor Orbán, contacted by the BBC, declined to comment.

An hour before polls closed in Serbia, masked and hooded vigilantes took up position in central Belgrade. During voting, similar groups were photographed at many polling stations, and blocked by election monitors.

There is another strange numerical similarity. The Student List will have 140 seats in the 250-seat Serbian parliament, the same number Péter Magyar's Tisza party won in the 199-seat Hungarian parliament.
Magyar was the only European leader to ring the students directly to congratulate them that evening - and probably the only one who had their number.
body_zh: 去年11月，当塞尔维亚总统亚历山大·武契奇和匈牙利总理维克多·欧尔班在塞尔维亚北部会面时，他们几乎没有想到他们会在一年内双双下台。
两人都被民众运动赶下台——欧尔班首先于四月下台，被彼得·马扎尔领导的蒂萨党击败。然后上周日，一个成立不到两年的学生运动以压倒性优势赢得了塞尔维亚议会选举。
匈牙利的蒂萨党和塞尔维亚的学生名单看起来非常不同——蒂萨党以其领导人的个性和能量为中心，而塞尔维亚的学生则坚称他们没有领导权。
但匈牙利和塞尔维亚的投票率高达 79% 和 69%，这是由两国精通技术的年轻人推动的。他们使用人工智能工具来处理数据，识别投票威胁，并动员数以万计的选举监督员来防止执政党的恐吓和选举舞弊。
选民的动员和选举监督员的作用对两国反对派的胜利发挥了重要作用。
上周末，匈牙利DE公民行动组织向塞尔维亚派遣了70名选举监察员，与学生运动代表合作，视察了塞尔维亚北部伏伊伏丁那省的投票站。
夏天，甚至在选举之前，他们就举办了研讨会，与塞尔维亚学生分享匈牙利选举的经验和方法。
一项关键技术是提前识别“受感染”的投票区——在之前的选举中，执政党得票数惊人的高的地方表明选民使用了恐吓或“连锁投票”技术。
“从选举日 16:00 左右开始，我们注意到一群蒙面流氓 - Vučiċ 支持者 - 聚集在投票站附近，”来自苏博蒂察的学生活动人士彼得·克莱姆 (Péter Klemm) 告诉 BBC。 “所以我们派出了机动小组，开始拍摄一切。”
他认为，结合已经到位的“固定”监控器，每个受到威胁的投票站都有 20 至 30 名志愿者，起到了强大的威慑作用，并防止了恐吓或欺诈。
匈牙利的欧尔班、塞尔维亚的武契奇，看起来都是所向披靡。两人都是强大的领导人，分别在位16年和14年，接管了国家机构并建立了覆盖两国的商业帝国。
大约一年前，奥尔班在苏博蒂察市中心一家受欢迎的小型面包店坐下来享用传统的 burek 糕点时，选择了奶酪和 Vučiċ 肉。
他们继续前往当地一家酿酒厂，谈论石油和其他商业交易——匈牙利计划购买塞尔维亚的尼什炼油厂。这两位民族主义领导人在商业和政治方面有很多共同点，尤其是他们与俄罗斯弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平的友谊，以及对波斯尼亚塞族分离主义领导人米洛拉德·多迪克的大力支持。
贝尔格莱德和布达佩斯之间的高速铁路正在由中国的资金和技术建造。
两人的权力倒台之间有着非同寻常的相似之处。亚历山大·武契奇 (Aleksandar Vučiċ) 在周日晚上 21:30 整承认失败，正如维克多·欧尔班 (Viktor Orbán) 在 4 月 12 日所做的那样。很少有观察家预计两位领导人会和平让步。
本周有人猜测，武契奇在周日晚上两次与欧尔班通话征求他的建议——一次是在他认输之前，另一次是在 23:15。欧尔班说服他的塞尔维亚盟友不要使用武力。
武契奇否认他在宣布这一消息之前曾与欧尔班进行过交谈，但承认了后来的谈话。 BBC 联系了维克托·欧尔班 (Viktor Orbán)，但他拒绝置评。
塞尔维亚投票结束前一小时，戴着面具和头巾的治安维持者在贝尔格莱德市中心占据了位置。投票期间，类似的群体在许多投票站被拍到，并被选举监视器封锁。
还有另一个奇怪的数字相似性。学生名单将在塞尔维亚议会250个席位中占据140个席位，与彼得·马扎尔领导的蒂萨党在匈牙利议会199个席位中赢得的席位相同。
马扎尔是当晚唯一一位直接给学生打电话向他们表示祝贺的欧洲领导人，而且可能是唯一一位知道学生电话号码的领导人。

title_en: India's opposition set to hold mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
title_zh: 印度反对派将举行大型集会寻求选举主席辞职
summary: It comes amid growing protests over a voter roll revision exercise feared to leave 130 million voters off rolls.
summary_zh: 此举正值选民名册修改活动引发越来越多的抗议，担心选民名册修改将导致 1.3 亿选民被剔除。
body_en: Tens of thousands of people are expected to gather in the Indian capital, Delhi, for a mega opposition rally, seeking the resignation of chief election commissioner and electoral reforms.
The rally, called by the main opposition Congress party, will begin around noon at the famous Ramlila Maidan grounds, with leaders claiming a million people could attend.
Several top leaders of the Congress-led INDIA alliance have said they would attend and the influential Gen Z-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has also pledged support.
The rally comes amid growing criticism of a voter-list revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from the draft rolls across India.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) says the exercise is aimed at updating the voters' list by purging names of people who have died or moved away from their registered addresses.

But opposition parties allege that the exercise - known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) - could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing eligible voters from the rolls. They accuse the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the BJP of "vote chori (theft)". Both the BJP and the ECI have denied the allegations.

The controversy intensified in September when The Indian Express newspaper in its investigation , external reported that the CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, made key decisions related to the exercise without the agreement of the two other election commissioners, who had raised objections on more than a dozen occasions.
The Election Commission said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.
But concerns over the revision process have continued, with the opposition parties, the CJP and student groups organising a number of protests in Delhi and other Indian cities.

Last month, Congress MP and leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi led tens of thousands of protesters in a march from Connaught Place in central Delhi to the Supreme Court, seeking the CEC's resignation.
"The march was just the trailer," a party leader told the BBC, adding that "Sunday's rally will be several times bigger than that".

Ahead of the rally, Gandhi said their protest was against "the demolition of Indian democracy", adding that "all the opposition parties and everybody who wants to come, political or non-political, is welcome".
"There is huge anger, huge emotional pain because millions are being disenfranchised," he said.
"We are all standing together because we are defending the Constitution. We are defending the idea of India. We are defending the vote, which is the expression of all Indians."

Delhi police have given permission to hold Sunday's rally, but it comes with several conditions. Media reports say the rally must end by 5pm, CCTV cameras must be installed at the venue and no marches will be allowed outside the designated protest site.
The planned mega rally has also divided opinion among traders in Chandni Chowk, one of Delhi's oldest and busiest markets, located less than a kilometre from Ramlila Maidan.
Earlier this week, a group of traders said the protest could hurt business during the festive season, coming just a week before Diwali.
But a rival group of traders said they supported Gandhi's rally and criticised the BJP for taking out a march through the market on Thursday, saying that disrupted the festive season more.
Authorities have deployed thousands of police and paramilitary personnel across the city, including the roads leading up to Ramlila Grounds, Sunday's protest venue.
The opposition, which has been preparing for the rally for days now, has accused the government of trying to stop people from travelling to Delhi to take part in the protest.
body_zh: 预计数万人将聚集在印度首都德里，举行大型反对派集会，寻求首席选举专员辞职和选举改革。
这次集会由主要反对党国大党号召，将于中午前后在著名的拉姆利拉迈丹广场开始，领导人声称将有一百万人参加。
国大党领导的印度联盟的几位高层领导人已表示将出席，Z 世代领导的颇具影响力的压力组织蟑螂党 (CJP) 也承诺支持。
这次集会正值印度选民名单修改行动受到越来越多的批评之际，该行动已从印度各地的选秀名单中删除了 1.3 亿人的名字。
印度选举委员会（ECI）表示，此次活动的目的是通过删除已死亡或搬离登记地址的人的姓名来更新选民名单。
但反对党声称，这项被称为“特别强化修订”（SIR）的活动可能会通过将符合资格的选民从名册中剔除而使总理纳伦德拉·莫迪领导的印度人民党（BJP）受益。他们指责首席选举专员（CEC）和印度人民党“盗窃选票”。印度人民党和 ECI 均否认了这些指控。
9月，《印度快报》在调查中对外报道称，中央选举委员会Gyanesh Kumar在未征得其他两名选举委员同意的情况下做出了与此次演习相关的关键决定，而这两名选举委员已多次提出反对意见，争议进一步加剧。
选举委员会表示，意见分歧在任何机构都是正常现象，不会影响其运作。
但对修订进程的担忧仍在继续，反对党、印度人民党和学生团体在德里和其他印度城市组织了多次抗议活动。
上个月，国大党议员兼反对党领袖拉胡尔·甘地率领数万名抗议者从德里市中心的康诺特广场游行至最高法院，要求中央选举委员会辞职。
一位政党领导人告诉英国广播公司：“游行只是预告片”，并补充说“周日的集会规模将是其数倍”。
集会前，甘地表示，他们的抗议是反对“摧毁印度民主”，并补充说“欢迎所有反对党和所有愿意参加的人，无论是政治的还是非政治的”。
他说：“人们感到巨大的愤怒和巨大的情感痛苦，因为数百万人被剥夺了权利。”
“我们都站在一起，因为我们正在捍卫宪法。我们正在捍卫印度的理念。我们正在捍卫投票，这是所有印度人的表达。”
德里警方已批准举行周日的集会，但有几个条件。媒体报道称，集会必须在下午5点前结束，集会地点必须安装闭路电视摄像机，并且不允许在指定抗议地点外进行游行。
计划中的大型集会也在月光集市（Chandni Chowk）的交易者之间产生了分歧。月光集市是德里最古老、最繁忙的市场之一，距离拉姆利拉迈丹 (Ramlila Maidan) 不到一公里。
本周早些时候，一群贸易商表示，抗议活动可能会损害排灯节前一周的节日期间的生意。
但另一群交易员表示，他们支持甘地的集会，并批评印度人民党周四在市场举行游行，称这对节日季节造成了更大的干扰。
当局在全市部署了数千名警察和准军事人员，包括通往周日抗议地点拉姆利拉广场的道路。
几天来一直在为集会做准备的反对派指责政府试图阻止人们前往德里参加抗议活动。

Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe Close
Hundreds of thousands of protesters demonstrated across France as the country prepares for a general strike in the coming days.
In Paris, police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in a third weekend of nationwide demonstrations against the rising cost of living and poor public services.
More than 320,000 people took to the streets around the country and at least 290 protesters were arrested, according to France's interior ministry. Police say about 70,000 demonstrated in Paris.
The authorities prepared extensively to avoid a repeat of the violence, rioting and looting that happened two weeks ago.
Protests also took place in Albania, Germany and Italy as youth take to the streets across Europe, the BBC's correspondent James Waterhouse reports.

title_en: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
title_zh: 在俄罗斯占领的前线城市生活多年后，乌克兰人说：“我们从地狱回来了”
summary: One evacuated couple says they crossed minefields in Oleshky in search of food.
summary_zh: 一对被疏散的夫妇说，他们穿过奥列什基的雷区寻找食物。
body_en: By Mariana Matveichuk , Reporting from Chernihiv and Amy Walker
Warning: This story contains graphic content.
Olha has one word to describe what life has been like in the front-line city of Oleshky over the past few years: "Horror".
Disembarking alongside her from a coach in the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv with their immediate family and dog, her husband Viacheslav put it this way: "We came back from hell."

The couple were among hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city who crossed into northern Ukraine via Belarus on Saturday, many reuniting with loved ones they had not seen for years.
Oleshky, seized by Russia during the first few days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River and on the other side by Russian forces.

Olha and Viacheslav had lived there with their son and daughter, both in their 30s. Even as the shelling around them intensified, they feared that trying to escape could be even more dangerous, with routes mined and subject to drone attack.

As supplies dwindled, the couple said they made an attempt to find food by crossing through minefields earlier this month. "People were stepping on mines, dying and being maimed, all just to survive," Olha told the BBC.
Those who were too afraid to go out in the city had resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive.
"We saw that the situation wasn't getting any better, so we realised we had to get out," Olha said.

That opportunity came earlier this week when a humanitarian ceasefire, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, took effect in the Kherson region, providing the first few days of peace in the area for four years and allowing Oleshky residents to evacuate.
Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, were believed to still be living in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, with 1,700 in the city itself.
Residents had a four-hour window on Friday to leave, with a convoy of 25 buses brought in for up to 750 evacuees, along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.
After travelling through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, then flying to Belarus, evacuees arrived on buses to a military facility in Chernihiv on Saturday.
On the tarmac, where evacuees were processed before travelling onwards, some elderly residents were so weak they had to be carried on stretchers.
As Mykhailo Palii arrived, his daughters Dasha and Anya, who thought they might never see him again, sprinted across the tarmac screaming and crying.
After an emotional embrace, Palii described a glimpse of life in Oleshky, although he said he had, until then, kept many of the details from his family.
"A hole was blown into the bathroom," he said. "There were drone attacks and missile strikes. It happened, but I didn't tell them about it because I knew they would worry."

Tetiana and Volodymyr, a couple carrying a cat when they arrived in Chernihiv, said their entire home was burned down three years ago, and they had been living in the abandoned house of a neighbour since.

For them, leaving as soon as it was safe to do so was an easy decision. "There's nothing for us to regret leaving. We don't have relatives there. Our children are married and don't live with us in the city," said Tetiana.
body_zh: 作者：Mariana Matveichuk，切尔尼戈夫和艾米·沃克报道
警告：这个故事包含图形内容。
奥尔哈用一个词来形容过去几年奥列什基一线城市的生活：“恐怖”。
与她一起从乌克兰切尔尼戈夫地区的一辆长途汽车上下来的时候，她的丈夫维亚切斯拉夫带着直系亲属和狗，这样说道：“我们从地狱回来了。”
这对夫妇是周六从俄罗斯占领的城市撤离的数百名居民之一，他们于周六经白俄罗斯进入乌克兰北部，其中许多人与多年未见的亲人团聚。
奥列什基在 2022 年 2 月全面入侵的头几天被俄罗斯占领，一侧被第聂伯河围困，另一侧被俄罗斯军队围困。
奥尔哈 (Olha) 和维亚切斯拉夫 (Viacheslav) 带着他们的儿子和女儿住在那里，他们都是 30 多岁。尽管周围的炮击愈演愈烈，他们还是担心试图逃跑可能会更加危险，因为路线上布满了地雷，而且容易受到无人机袭击。
随着供应减少，这对夫妇表示，他们本月早些时候试图穿过雷区寻找食物。奥尔哈告诉英国广播公司：“人们踩到地雷，要么死亡，要么受伤，这一切只是为了生存。”
那些不敢进城的人只能靠煮菜园里的杂草来维持生计。
“我们看到情况没有任何好转，所以我们意识到我们必须离开，”奥尔哈说。
本周早些时候，这个机会来了，在美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普的斡旋下，人道主义停火在赫尔松地区生效，为该地区带来了四年来最初几天的和平，并允许奥列什基居民撤离。
据信仍有多达 6,000 人（其中包括 200 名儿童）居住在奥列什基及其周边地区，其中 1,700 人居住在该市。
周五，居民有四个小时的时间离开，一支由 25 辆巴士组成的车队运载了多达 750 名疏散人员，并为行动不便的人提供了救护车。
经过俄罗斯占领的领土前往俄罗斯南部，然后飞往白俄罗斯后，撤离人员于周六乘坐巴士抵达切尔尼戈夫的一处军事设施。
在停机坪上，疏散人员在继续前行之前接受了处理，一些老年居民非常虚弱，不得不用担架抬着。
当米凯洛·帕利到达时，他的女儿达莎和安雅以为自己可能再也见不到他了，尖叫着哭着冲过停机坪。
在一次激动人心的拥抱之后，帕利描述了奥列什基生活的一瞥，尽管他说在那之前他一直向家人隐瞒了许多细节。
“浴室被炸了一个洞，”他说。 “发生了无人机袭击和导弹袭击。这种事确实发生了，但我没有告诉他们，因为我知道他们会担心。”
Tetiana 和 Volodymyr 是一对夫妇，他们抵达切尔尼戈夫时带着一只猫。他们说，三年前他们的整个房子都被烧毁了，从那以后他们就一直住在邻居的废弃房子里。
对他们来说，在安全的情况下尽快离开是一个简单的决定。 “离开没有什么让我们后悔的。我们在那里没有亲戚。我们的孩子已经结婚了，不和我们一起住在城里，”特蒂亚娜说。

title_en: Thousands rally in Israel urging Eisenkot-Arab deal to remove Netanyahu
title_zh: 以色列数千人集会敦促艾森科特与阿拉伯达成协议以罢免内塔尼亚胡
summary: In a counterprotest, Netanyahu supporters demand that Israel should not have a government with 'terrorists'.
summary_zh: 作为反抗议，内塔尼亚胡的支持者要求以色列不应该有一个有“恐怖分子”的政府。
body_en: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu | Benjamin Netanyahu News | Al Jazeera
Share Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu on social media
Thousands of people have rallied in Tel Aviv to urge the Israeli opposition to make a deal with Arab parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Protesters at Saturday’s rally told the AFP news agency this may be the “last chance for real change” and that Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, is a “great manipulator”.

Main opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has previously ruled out forming a coalition with Israel’s Arab parties, but a deadlock in Tuesday’s elections means siding with the parties could help him form a government.

“People really want this vote for change to work out, and they believe that… Gadi Eisenkot and other leaders of the Jewish-Israeli parties need to listen to their voice,” Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh said from Ramallah on Saturday.

Counter-protesters also showed up to Saturday’s demonstrations, with Netanyahu supporters seen shouting their own demands that “Israel should not have a government with so-called terrorists”, Odeh said.
Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday’s elections, while Eisenkot’s won 48, meaning neither side can form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament alone.
Israel’s three Arab-led parties won 19 seats, having made significant gains in Tuesday’s election.
Nearly 840,000 people voted for Ra’am and the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab-led parties, a 64 percent increase from the last elections in 2022, according to the Central Election Committee.
The Arab electoral success means a coalition with Eisenkot would provide a comfortable majority of 67. However, for many in Israel, the idea of siding with Arabs is politically unpalatable.
Netanyahu has accused Palestinian-Israeli parties of “stealing” the polls and accepting funding from Qatar to do it. Qatar has rejected the allegations , calling it a disinformation campaign.

Odeh said that Israeli right-wing circles have described “the historic turnout of Palestinian Israelis as electoral terrorism, equating it to the October 7th attack”, when Hamas-led fighters stormed southern Israel, killing more than 1,200 people and taking hundreds captive.
“Palestinian-Israeli votes and voices” are under attack because they have a “prominent position” in deciding whether Eisenkot can form a government, she added.
body_zh: 以色列数千人集会敦促“犹太-阿拉伯”联盟推翻内塔尼亚胡本杰明·内塔尼亚胡新闻|半岛电视台
以色列数千人集会在社交媒体上敦促“犹太-阿拉伯”联盟推翻内塔尼亚胡
数千人在特拉维夫集会，敦促以色列反对派与阿拉伯政党达成协议，罢免总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡。
周六集会上的抗议者告诉法新社，这可能是“真正变革的最后机会”，以色列任期最长的总理内塔尼亚胡是一个“伟大的操纵者”。
主要反对党领袖加迪·艾森科特此前曾排除与以色列阿拉伯政党组建联盟的可能性，但周二选举陷入僵局意味着站在各政党一边可能有助于他组建政府。
“人们真的希望这次变革投票能够成功，他们相信……加迪·艾森科特和犹太以色列政党的其他领导人需要倾听他们的声音，”半岛电视台记者努尔·奥德周六在拉马拉表示。
奥德说，反抗议者也出现在周六的示威活动中，内塔尼亚胡的支持者高喊着自己的要求，即“以色列不应该有一个由所谓恐怖分子组成的政府”。
内塔尼亚胡的阵营在周二的选举中赢得了 53 个席位，而艾森科特的阵营则赢得了 48 个席位，这意味着双方都无法单独在以色列 120 个席位的议会中组建政府。
以色列三个阿拉伯领导的政党赢得了 19 个席位，在周二的选举中取得了重大进展。
根据中央选举委员会的数据，近 84 万人投票支持拉姆和联合名单（由三个阿拉伯领导的政党组成的联盟），比 2022 年上次选举增加了 64%。
阿拉伯人在选举中取得成功意味着与艾森科特组成的联盟将获得 67 席的多数席位。然而，对于许多以色列人来说，站在阿拉伯人一边的想法在政治上是令人难以接受的。
内塔尼亚胡指责巴勒斯坦-以色列政党“窃取”民意调查并接受卡塔尔的资助来做到这一点。卡塔尔否认了这些指控，称其为虚假信息活动。
奥德表示，以色列右翼圈子将“巴勒斯坦以色列人的历史性投票称为选举恐怖主义，将其等同于 10 月 7 日的袭击”，当时哈马斯领导的武装分子袭击了以色列南部，造成 1,200 多人死亡，数百人被俘。
她补充说，“巴以的选票和声音”受到攻击，因为他们在决定艾森科特能否组建政府方面拥有“突出地位”。

body_en: France is bracing for a third consecutive weekend of protests, with around 70,000 security personnel deployed to prevent a repeat of the violence seen on October 17. Shops have boarded up their premises as authorities warn of further clashes, with Halloween celebrations adding to security concerns over masked demonstrators. The protests, involving Yellow Vest activists, trade unions and students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality and poor school conditions, but have since expanded to include demands for greater civil liberties and the right to protest. The demonstrations come six months ahead of presidential elections, amid a tense political climate and growing support for the far right. Authorities have restricted marches in several cities, while Paris police have only authorised a demonstration on the capital's outskirts. Curfews have also been imposed in parts of Paris as officials seek to prevent further unrest.

body_en: Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected

Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.

Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. With wind gusts in excess of 85mph (140km/h) and rainfall totals in some regions exceeding 200mm, the severe storm has prompted mass evacuations of more than 180,000 people, as well as widespread disruption to energy and transport infrastructure. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.

title_en: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
title_zh: 加密货币公司 Binance 承担 63 亿美元黑客攻击后 90% 的损失
summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says North Korea was responsible for the hack.
summary_zh: 美国联邦调查局 (FBI) 表示，朝鲜应对此次黑客攻击负责。
body_en: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.
The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added.
Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so.
"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the hack.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.
Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.
All holdings of the cryptocurrencies bitcoin, ethereum and Tether are covered, along with seven other widely-traded crypto assets, the company said.
From Bitcoin to Binance: Crypto terms and what they mean

The company said its next goal is resuming withdrawal services for users, saying it remained on track to reopen withdrawals on Sunday 1 November and would provide a further update once details were confirmed.
The hack is believed to be the largest in history, eclipsing the record of a $1.5bn heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025 - for which the FBI also said North Korea was responsible.
North Korea has always denied involvement in these attacks.

Binance's initial investigation suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, which allowed access to unauthorised withdrawals, but a later update said they had uncovered "additional points of breach".

Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, said the hack was carried out by more than one person, and the hackers used sophisticated methods to hide their tracks, such as a "self-destruct mechanism".
On Friday, the company said it had frozen around $3bn of stolen assets after working with law enforcement, intelligence firms and partners.

The investigation is ongoing, it added. The US Secret Service said on Friday it is "working around the clock" with private sector partners "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds" stolen from Binance.
Binance, founded in China in 2017, lets users buy, sell and trade digital assets - it is estimated to have hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
Crypto is a digital asset, which doesn't exist physically and is instead accessed via digital wallets or computers.
Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far

body_zh: 全球最大的加密货币交易所币安表示，周四在一次黑客攻击中被盗的 63 亿美元（47 亿英镑）资产中的 90% 已得到赔偿。
该公司补充说，剩下的 10% 可能需要更长时间才能获得所需数量。
币安一直承诺将承担 100% 的损失，该损失被怀疑是有史以来最大的加密货币黑客攻击，并表示已拨出超过 63.4 亿美元的公司资金来做到这一点。
该公司在周六的一份声明中表示：“币安将承担这些被盗资金的财务影响，而不是我们的用户。”
美国联邦调查局 (FBI) 周六表示，朝鲜应对此次黑客攻击负责。
两家分析公司此前告诉 BBC，他们掌握的可靠情报表明，朝鲜国家支持的黑客组织 Lazarus Group（也称为 TraderTraitor）可能是罪魁祸首。
币安表示，它已使用各种资金和自己的公司财务补充了被盗的资产。
该公司表示，所有持有的加密货币比特币、以太坊和 Tether 以及其他七种广泛交易的加密资产都包含在内。
从比特币到币安：加密术语及其含义
该公司表示，其下一个目标是恢复为用户提供提款服务，并表示仍有望在 11 月 1 日星期日重新开放提款，并将在细节确认后提供进一步的更新。
此次黑客攻击被认为是历史上规模最大的一次，打破了 2025 年 Bybit 交易所被盗 15 亿美元的记录，而联邦调查局 (FBI) 也表示朝鲜对此负有责任。
朝鲜一直否认参与了这些袭击。
币安的初步调查显示，一名工程师的笔记本电脑遭到入侵，导致未经授权的提款行为，但后来的更新称，他们发现了“其他漏洞”。
币安联席首席执行官理查德·滕（Richard Teng）表示，这次黑客攻击是由不止一个人实施的，黑客使用了复杂的方法来隐藏自己的踪迹，例如“自毁机制”。
周五，该公司表示，在与执法部门、情报公司和合作伙伴合作后，已冻结了约 30 亿美元的被盗资产。
它补充说，调查正在进行中。美国特勤局周五表示，它正在与私营部门合作伙伴“昼夜不停地工作”，以“识别、冻结、追踪和追回”从币安被盗的资金。
币安于 2017 年在中国成立，允许用户购买、出售和交易数字资产 - 据估计在全球拥有数亿用户。
加密货币是一种数字资产，它并不实际存在，而是通过数字钱包或计算机访问。
谁可能是币安黑客事件的幕后黑手以及我们目前所知的情况

title_en: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
title_zh: 西班牙火车灾难给桑切斯连任的机会蒙上阴影
summary: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.
summary_zh: 距离提前大选仅几周，西班牙首相遭遇一系列危机。
body_en: Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent , Reporting from Toledo
The breaking news from Spain this week was shocking but also shockingly familiar: another collision on the high-speed rail line south from Madrid, with reports of dozens killed.
It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people. Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment.
For the victims' families it is devastating; a personal tragedy.

But it is also a national disaster that has shattered confidence in the country's rail network and the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez. It is playing out just weeks before the snap general election he called.
The formal investigation into the Toledo train disaster has only just been launched but the government has been quick to take control of the narrative.
From the first hours after the collision, Transport Minister Oscar Puente began suggesting "human error" was to blame, batting responsibility as far as possible from the cabinet.
On Friday, he appeared before the press for a second time to set out what he called the "objective facts" of the crash and counter a surge of criticism against the government.
The opposition People's Party (PP) is among those calling for his resignation as a "moral" and "ethical" move.
Instead after expressing "huge pain and sadness" for the victims, Puente went on the offensive.
He rejected talk of chronic underinvestment in infrastructure and insisted that Spain's high-speed signalling safety system, the LZB, was neither old nor inadequate: Germany and Austria use the same.
In Spain, it has already failed 170 times so far this year, he revealed, but called that "normal" and around the EU average.
The problem surrounds what happens next - when the system fails and control of the line shifts to manual.
In this case, the minister highlighted a series of human errors that proved catastrophic.
Crucially, at one point a controller instructed a stalled train to restart, clearing it to advance at up to 160km/h (100 mph) even though a second train was stuck on the line up ahead.
The impending collision was clear from audio calls and on big screens in the control centre in Madrid.
"They worked. We checked. They could see what was happening," Puente confirmed. But the advancing train was never ordered to stop.
So would he take personal and political responsibility anyway, and resign? Puente called it his "duty", rather, to remain as minister.
"I'll face up to things, explain, elucidate," he countered. "I'll think how to improve the system, and give confidence to those who want to travel by train and feel calm and safe."
"This is not only a very serious accident, but the second in a very short time," Paco Camas of the pollster Ipsos points out.
body_zh: 南欧和东欧记者，托莱多报道
本周来自西班牙的突发新闻令人震惊，但也令人震惊地熟悉：马德里以南的高铁线上再次发生碰撞，据报道有数十人死亡。
距离科尔多瓦附近两列火车相撞、造成 46 人死亡仅九个月。目前，西班牙中部已从散布在铁轨和路堤上的残骸中找到了 69 具尸体。
对于受害者家属来说，这是毁灭性的；个人悲剧。
但这也是一场全国性灾难，粉碎了人们对该国铁路网络和佩德罗·桑切斯领导的社会党政府的信心。就在他呼吁提前大选的几周前，这场比赛即将上演。
对托莱多火车灾难的正式调查才刚刚启动，但政府很快就控制了局势。
从碰撞发生后的最初几个小时起，交通部长奥斯卡·普恩特就开始暗示“人为失误”是事故的罪魁祸首，并尽可能地推卸内阁的责任。
周五，他第二次出现在媒体面前，阐述了他所谓的坠机事件的“客观事实”，并反驳了针对政府的批评浪潮。
反对党人民党是呼吁他辞职的人士之一，认为这是“道德”和“道德”的举动。
在向受害者表达“巨大的痛苦和悲伤”后，普恩特转而采取攻势。
他否认了基础设施投资长期不足的说法，并坚称西班牙的高速信号安全系统 LZB 既不陈旧也不不足：德国和奥地利也使用同样的系统。
他透露，今年迄今为止，西班牙已经失败了 170 次，但他称这“正常”，接近欧盟平均水平。
问题围绕着接下来会发生什么——当系统发生故障并且生产线的控制转为手动时。
在这种情况下，部长强调了一系列被证明是灾难性的人为错误。
至关重要的是，在某一时刻，管制员指示一列停滞的列车重新启动，使其以 160 公里/小时（100 英里/小时）的速度前进，尽管前面有第二列列车被困在线路上。
从音频通话和马德里控制中心的大屏幕上可以清楚地看到即将发生的碰撞。
“他们工作了。我们检查了。他们可以看到发生了什么，”普恩特证实。但行进中的火车从未被命令停止。
那么他无论如何都会承担个人和政治责任并辞职吗？普恩特称其为“职责”，更确切地说，是继续担任部长。
“我会面对事情，解释，阐明，”他反驳道。 “我会思考如何改进这个系统，给那些想要乘坐火车旅行并感到平静和安全的人信心。”
民意调查机构益普索 (Ipsos) 的帕科·卡马斯 (Paco Camas) 指出：“这不仅是一次非常严重的事故，而且是短时间内的第二起事故。”

title_zh: 加拿大和欧盟宣布新联盟向志同道合的国家开放
summary: Alliance for the Future, unveiled at Montreal summit and open to other countries, conceived for world ‘shaken by new storms’ Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens c
summary_zh: 未来联盟在蒙特利尔峰会上揭晓并向其他国家开放，为“被新风暴震撼”的世界构想加拿大和欧洲有一个
body_en: Canada and EU announce new alliance open to like-minded countries
Alliance for the Future, unveiled at Montreal summit and open to other countries, conceived for world ‘shaken by new storms’

Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join.

Speaking to reporters on Friday from Montreal, the prime minister, Mark Carney, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , called the new partnership the Alliance for the Future and said the “deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc had the potential to offer unprecedented stability and opportunity”.

“Our societies have been shaken by new storms,” Carney told reporters, referring to the damaging effects of the climate emergency but also the “erosion of democratic norms” and “the weaponization of trade”.

As they concluded their two-day summit, Canada agreed to contribute to a €90bn support loan for Ukraine. Leaders also said future discussions would lead to a more integrated market worth tens of billions of dollars, reduced trade and travel restrictions, and new educational opportunities for both sides.

While a trade war between Canada and the United States has seen Carney go hunting for new geopolitical partners, an over-reliance on American companies – especially for defence – has also given Canada pause.
Last week, Elon Musk throttled the speeds of Starlink and Starshield over Ukraine in mid-October, severely disrupting Ukrainian military and defense operations.

Carney has repeatedly raised the concern that Canada’s defense technologies could be at the whim of political actors or companies with opposing interests. Musk, a dual Canadian citizen, is a critic of Canada’s governing Liberal party and has advocated for provinces to separate.

Carney pointed to a planned merger between the Canadian artificial intelligence company Cohere Inc and Germany’s Aleph Alpha GmbH as a step to lessening reliance on American AI giants. The tie-up will see the newly formed company have dual headquarters in Berlin and Toronto, and Canada’s federal government has announced a stake in Cohere worth up to C$1.6bn.
“We are not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don’t know, or by whom we don’t trust,” Carney said on Thursday.
Brussels and Ottawa also announced an agreement on Friday that would bringing Canada into Europe’s supercomputing network, giving Canadian access to European machines to train AI models.

In addition to lofty promises of helping to reshape the global order, or giving safe harbour to like-minded nations looking to weather uncertainty, Canadian and EU leaders also pitched their new, deeper relationship as one that addressed key sources of anxiety for residents, including the cost of living.

“When trade becomes a tool of economic pressure, it’s the families that pay the price, from the supermarket shelf to the cost of a new car,” Von der Leyen said, noting that previously trusted suppliers of energy, critical minerals or semiconductors “are increasingly turned into instruments of pressure”.
“More competition, more choice,” Carney said earlier in the day, suggesting the alliance could find ways to build certainty around supply chains and “withstand shocks, together”.

The leaders once again brought up the prospect of Canada becoming an associate member. The designation is uncharted territory, said Von der Leyen, who added: “We have the ambition, trust, and creativity to shape it together.
“This [associate membership] is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength.”

While the leaders committed to the idea of associate membership, they said a clearer scope of the role would come at a 2027 summit. Some EU members had bristled at the idea of Canada being given a legally meaningless designation that they fear confuses other nations looking for membership. Germany and other states had worked behind the scenes to remove the phrase from a draft of the summit statement. But Von der Leyen, who first floated the term, and Carney both again referred to “associate membership” at the summit.

European Council president Antonio Costa, meanwhile, said earlier that Canada was “by far the most European of the non-European countries”, a sentiment that reflected a belief that despite geography, there was a collective sense of shared values.
Costa said the two sides would pursue “the most closer, the most deepest, the most stronger association ever between European Union and a non-European country”.
body_zh: 加拿大和欧盟宣布新联盟向志同道合的国家开放
未来联盟在蒙特利尔峰会上揭晓并向其他国家开放，为“被新风暴震撼的世界”构想
加拿大和欧洲宣布成立一个由志同道合的国家组成的新联盟，既作为“我们公民得以繁荣发展的保护伞”，又作为抵御地缘政治不可预测性的有力对冲，同时欢迎其他国家加入。
周五，加拿大总理马克·卡尼和欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩在蒙特利尔对记者发表讲话，称这一新伙伴关系为“未来联盟”，并表示“加拿大与这个由 27 个成员国组成的集团之间尽可能深入的伙伴关系有可能提供前所未有的稳定和机会”。
卡尼对记者说：“我们的社会已经被新的风暴所震撼。”他指的是气候紧急情况的破坏性影响，以及“民主规范的侵蚀”和“贸易武器化”。
在结束为期两天的峰会时，加拿大同意向乌克兰提供 900 亿欧元的支持贷款。领导人还表示，未来的讨论将带来价值数百亿美元的更加一体化的市场、减少贸易和旅行限制，并为双方提供新的教育机会。
虽然加拿大和美国之间的贸易战让卡尼开始寻找新的地缘政治合作伙伴，但对美国公司的过度依赖——尤其是在国防领域——也让加拿大犹豫不决。
上周，埃隆·马斯克于十月中旬降低了“星链”和“星盾”在乌克兰上空的速度，严重扰乱了乌克兰的军事和国防行动。
卡尼一再表示担心，加拿大的国防技术可能会受到政治参与者或利益相反的公司的一时兴起的影响。马斯克拥有加拿大双重国籍，他批评加拿大执政的自由党，并主张各省分开。
卡尼指出，加拿大人工智能公司 Cohere Inc 和德国 Aleph Alpha GmbH 计划合并，以此作为减少对美国人工智能巨头依赖的一步。此次合作将使新成立的公司在柏林和多伦多设有双总部，加拿大联邦政府已宣布将持有 Cohere 价值高达 16 亿加元的股份。
卡尼周四表示：“我们不会等待人工智能的未来由我们不认识的人或我们不信任的人在其他地方决定。”
布鲁塞尔和渥太华周五还宣布了一项协议，将加拿大纳入欧洲超级计算网络，让加拿大能够使用欧洲机器来训练人工智能模型。
除了帮助重塑全球秩序或为志同道合的国家提供安全港以应对不确定性的崇高承诺外，加拿大和欧盟领导人还宣传他们新的、更深入的关系，以解决居民焦虑的主要根源，包括生活成本。
冯德莱恩表示：“当贸易成为经济压力的工具时，付出代价的就是家庭，从超市货架到新车的成本。”他指出，以前值得信赖的能源、关键矿产或半导体供应商“越来越多地变成了压力工具”。
卡尼当天早些时候表示，“更多竞争，更多选择”，并暗示该联盟可以找到围绕供应链建立确定性并“共同抵御冲击”的方法。
领导人再次提出加拿大成为准成员的前景。冯德莱恩表示，这一称号是一个未知的领域，他补充道：“我们有雄心、信任和创造力来共同塑造它。
“这种[准会员资格]是一种伙伴关系，不是针对任何其他人，而是为了我们的共同力量。”
虽然领导人致力于准会员的想法，但他们表示，更明确的角色范围将在 2027 年峰会上公布。一些欧盟成员国对加拿大被赋予一个在法律上毫无意义的称号的想法感到愤怒，他们担心这会让其他寻求加入欧盟的国家感到困惑。德国和其他国家在幕后努力从峰会声明草案中删除这句话。但最先提出这个词的冯德莱恩和卡尼在峰会上都再次提到了“准会员”。
与此同时，欧洲理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔早些时候表示，加拿大是“迄今为止最欧洲化的非欧洲国家”，这种情绪反映了一种信念，即尽管地理位置不同，但仍存在共同价值观的集体意识。
科斯塔表示，双方将寻求“欧盟与非欧洲国家之间有史以来最密切、最深入、最牢固的联系”。

title_en: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
title_zh: 刚果民主共和国最致命的埃博拉疫情造成 5,000 多人死亡
summary: Government data shows that more than 10,000 people have contracted the rare virus.
summary_zh: 政府数据显示，已有超过 10,000 人感染了这种罕见病毒。
body_en: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak - BBC News
More than 5,000 people have died from an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, government data shows.
Eight of 26 provinces are now affected, with more than 10,300 confirmed cases.
The outbreak, which started in May, became the country's deadliest in its history in August, public health officials said. The current case fatality rate is 48.6%.

In its latest update, the health ministry said the epicentre of the epidemic remains in the Ituri province, in the north-east of the country, which is a conflict zone, making it harder to contain the virus.
Cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.
This marks the 17th outbreak in DR Congo's history, according to the United Nations (UN), and the second largest in history.
The World Health Organization (WHO) office in Africa said a "continued scale-up of key control measures, greater access to affected areas, and community outreach" is needed to end the outbreak.
Testing and treatment are under way, along with clinical trials of vaccines, it added.
The Bundibugyo species is behind the current outbreak, but there is not yet any treatment or vaccine for this strain.
DR Congo's previous deadliest outbreak saw 2,299 deaths recorded between 2018-2020, the UN said.

The deadliest in history occurred in West Africa between 2014 and 2016, killing more than 11,325 people and spread across several countries, including Italy, the UK and United States, according to the WHO.
The UN warns that the current outbreak is "taking lives at a much faster rate".
Ebola is a rare, deadly disease caused by a virus, and symptoms come on suddenly.
As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.
The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
Adding to the challenge of treating the disease, some health workers and a politician have been attacked while responding to the outbreak.

Earlier this week, a nurse was killed and another health worker seriously injured in an attack when responding to an Ebola alert. Local youths had accused them of contaminating water sources and spreading the virus, according to the UN-backed Radio Okapi.

Last month, a politician was beaten to death after promoting measures to stop the spread of Ebola, while in August, the Red Cross said its volunteers had been injured and an ambulance set on fire in 11 violent incidents in the outbreak's first 100 days.

In Uganda, two people died and 20 cases were recorded shortly after the outbreak started, but no cases have been reported since August. Travel restrictions remain in place for those crossing into the country from neighbouring DR Congo.
body_zh: 刚果民主共和国最致命的埃博拉疫情造成 5,000 多人死亡 - BBC 新闻
政府数据显示，刚果民主共和国持续爆发的埃博拉疫情已造成 5000 多人死亡。
目前26个省份中有8个受到影响，确诊病例超过10,300例。
公共卫生官员表示，这场疫情始于五月，八月成为该国历史上最致命的一次。目前病死率为48.6%。
卫生部在最新的更新中表示，疫情的震中仍然是该国东北部的伊图里省，该省是一个冲突地区，使得控制该病毒变得更加困难。
肯尼亚、尼日利亚和乌干达也已确诊病例。
据联合国称，这是刚果民主共和国历史上第 17 次疫情爆发，也是历史上第二大疫情。
世界卫生组织（WHO）驻非洲办事处表示，需要“继续扩大关键控制措施、扩大受影响地区的准入范围并开展社区外展”，以结束疫情。
它补充说，测试和治疗以及疫苗的临床试验正在进行中。
Bundibugyo 物种是当前疫情爆发的幕后黑手，但目前还没有针对该菌株的任何治疗方法或疫苗。
联合国表示，2018 年至 2020 年期间，刚果民主共和国爆发了此前最致命的疫情，造成 2,299 人死亡。
据世界卫生组织称，2014 年至 2016 年间，历史上最严重的一场疫情发生在西非，造成超过 11,325 人死亡，疫情蔓延至意大利、英国和美国等多个国家。
联合国警告说，当前的疫情“正在以更快的速度夺走生命”。
埃博拉是一种由病毒引起的罕见致命疾病，症状突然出现。
随着疾病的进展，出现呕吐和腹泻，并可能导致器官衰竭。有些（但不是全部）患者会出现内出血和外出血。
病毒通过接触血液或呕吐物等受感染的体液从一个人传播到另一个人。
一些卫生工作者和一名政客在应对疫情时遭到袭击，这增加了治疗该疾病的挑战。
本周早些时候，在应对埃博拉警报时发生的袭击中，一名护士被杀，另一名卫生工作者受重伤。据联合国支持的霍加皮广播电台报道，当地年轻人指责他们污染水源并传播病毒。
上个月，一名政客在宣传阻止埃博拉病毒传播的措施后被殴打致死，而8月份，红十字会表示，在疫情爆发的前100天里，发生了11起暴力事件，其中有志愿者受伤，一辆救护车被纵火。
在乌干达，疫情爆发后不久，已有两人死亡并报告了 20 例病例，但自 8 月以来尚未报告任何病例。对于从邻国刚果民主共和国入境的人来说，旅行限制仍然存在。

summary_zh: 据估计，朝鲜按照自己的规则行事，盗窃加密货币的收入占该国外汇收入的一半。孤立的、秘密的
body_en: How crypto hacking funds isolated North Korea’s nuclear programme
Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate half of the country’s foreign currency income

North Korea plays by its own rules. The isolated, secretive and autocratic country is largely cut off from the world’s economic system – but when it comes to generating foreign earnings it relies on some of the world’s most sophisticated hacking.

Experts, such as TRM Labs, quickly attributed the extraordinary $6.3bn (£4.7bn) Binance cryptocurrency theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit that has also been known as the Lazarus Group. Though the link may not be proven yet, the pattern of behaviour is familiar.

North Korea has a history of cryptocurrency theft dating back to 2017, focusing on the sector’s relatively lax security controls as a way of stealing money and generating revenues for its military, including its nuclear weapons programme.

Kim Jong-un, its dictatorial ruler, controls a stockpile of about 50 nuclear warheads, and has been supplying troops and weapons to help Russia in its war in Ukraine. But North Korea is also extremely poor: 40% of the population are undernourished according to the UN and nearly one in five of its children are stunted.
North Korea is likely culprit behind $6.3bn crypto hack, ‘largest heist in history’

A UN panel of experts , reporting to the security council, said in the spring of 2024 that it was reviewing “58 suspected cyber-attacks” by North Korea “on cryptocurrency-related companies between 2017 and 2023” worth $3bn.

The panel said the cash was estimated to generate half of North Korea’s foreign currency income. One unnamed country went further with its estimate: the stolen billions fund “40% of the weapons of mass destruction programmes”.

The suspected crypto hacks amounted to as many as 17 in 2023 alone: thefts valued at $750m, and disturbingly, the sums involved are only increasing. The world’s largest previous crypto hack took place in February 2025, when $1.5bn was stolen from the Bybit exchange – the work, the FBI said, of TraderTraitor.

Ciaran Martin, a former head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre, argues that North Korea appears to have targeted crypto because traditional banks have developed sophisticated defences that the fast-growing and lightly regulated sector has yet to match.

“Over the last decade, hackers have walked off with nine- or 10-figure sums from crypto hacks on more than 30 occasions. The number of traditional banks who have suffered a loss of more than $100m as a result of a cyber-attack in the same period is zero or one,” Martin said.

North Korea was behind one of the last large cyber thefts on a traditional bank – an attack on Bangladesh Bank in February 2016, where North Korean hackers tried to illicitly move $951m from an account the bank had with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, taking advantage of time differences between the two.

A piece of luck prevented most of the money from being sent to an intermediate account in the Philippines. The corresponding bank was based on Jupiter Street, which shares its first word with the name of a sanctioned Iranian ship, so most of the transfers were held up. In the end, $81m was stolen.

The isolated state has long been accused of engaging in criminal activities to survive, including the forgery of high-quality $100 bills, known as “supernotes” in the 1990s, and the production and trafficking of crystal meth for export in the 2000s.

The UK has been rarely targeted. In 2019, North Korean hackers did try to take control of cash machines linked to 56 financial institutions to make them pay out sums well in excess of normal. British officials spotted what was afoot, alerted the banks and the hack was quietly suppressed with no media coverage.
How big a deal is the $6.3bn crypto heist, who did it, and are investments safe?

The irony is that the internet in North Korea is severely restricted, with access denied to the general population. Maths and science are pushed at school, however, and at university some of the best students are recruited into hacker groups, such as Lazarus, operating under the auspices of the country’s Reconnaissance General Bureau spy agency.

Hacking is closely tied to the all-powerful state. In December 2014, it emerged, to the embarrassment of Sony Pictures, that film stars Jennifer Lawrence and Amy Adams were paid less than their male counterparts in American Hustle. It was one of thousands of embarrassing emails leaked from the Hollywood studio through a hack.

The attack, by North Korea’s Lazarus Group , was conducted because Sony had funded a film, The Interview: a Seth Rogen comedy that depicted the assassination of Kim Jong-un. Amid the chaos of the revelations, Sony tried to cancel the movie, then had to U-turn on its retreat, releasing it online and to a handful of cinemas, after being criticised for caving in to North Korean pressure.
body_zh: 加密黑客资金如何隔离朝鲜的核计划
据估计，加密货币盗窃产生了该国一半的外汇收入
朝鲜按照自己的规则行事。这个孤立、神秘和独裁的国家在很大程度上与世界经济体系隔绝——但在创造外汇收入方面，它依赖于一些世界上最复杂的黑客活动。
TRM Labs 等专家很快将币安 63 亿美元（47 亿英镑）的加密货币盗窃案归咎于 TraderTraitor，这是一个朝鲜精英黑客组织，也被称为 Lazarus Group。尽管这种联系可能尚未得到证实，但其行为模式是熟悉的。
朝鲜的加密货币盗窃历史可以追溯到 2017 年，重点关注该行业相对宽松的安全控制，以此窃取资金并为其军队（包括其核武器计划）创收。
其独裁统治者金正恩控制着约50枚核弹头的库存，并一直在向俄罗斯提供军队和武器来帮助其在乌克兰的战争。但朝鲜也极其贫穷：根据联合国的数据，该国 40% 的人口营养不良，近五分之一的儿童发育迟缓。
朝鲜可能是价值 63 亿美元的加密货币黑客攻击的罪魁祸首，这是“历史上最大的盗窃案”
联合国专家小组在 2024 年春天向安理会报告时表示，正在审查朝鲜“在 2017 年至 2023 年间对加密货币相关公司发动的 58 起疑似网络攻击”，价值 30 亿美元。
该小组表示，这些现金估计占朝鲜外汇收入的一半。一个未透露姓名的国家进一步估计：被盗的数十亿美元资金用于“40%的大规模杀伤性武器计划”。
仅 2023 年一年，涉嫌加密货币黑客攻击的事件就多达 17 起：盗窃案价值达 7.5 亿美元，而且令人不安的是，涉案金额还在不断增加。此前全球最大规模的加密货币黑客攻击发生在 2025 年 2 月，当时 Bybit 交易所被盗 15 亿美元，FBI 称这是 TraderTraitor 所为。
英国国家网络安全中心前负责人夏兰·马丁 (Ciaran Martin) 认为，朝鲜似乎将加密货币作为目标，因为传统银行已经开发出复杂的防御措施，而快速增长且监管宽松的行业尚未与之匹敌。
“在过去的十年中，黑客已经通过加密货币黑客攻击窃取了 9 到 10 位数的 30 多次资金。同期因网络攻击而遭受 1 亿美元以上损失的传统银行数量为零或一家，”Martin 说道。
朝鲜是最近针对传统银行的大规模网络盗窃事件之一——2016 年 2 月对孟加拉国银行的攻击，朝鲜黑客试图利用两者之间的时差，从该银行在纽约联邦储备银行的账户中非法转移 9.51 亿美元。
幸运的是，大部分资金未能汇入菲律宾的一个中间账户。相应的银行位于木星街，该银行的第一个单词与一艘受制裁的伊朗船只的名称相同，因此大部分转账都被搁置。最终，8100 万美元被盗。
这个与世隔绝的国家长期以来一直被指控为生存而从事犯罪活动，包括在 2000 年代伪造高质量的 100 美元纸币（被称为“超级纸币”），以及在 2000 年代生产和贩运用于出口的冰毒。
英国很少成为攻击目标。 2019 年，朝鲜黑客确实试图控制与 56 家金融机构相关的提款机，使它们支付远远超出正常水平的金额。英国官员发现了正在发生的事情，并向银行发出了警报，这次黑客攻击被悄悄地压制住了，没有媒体报道。
价值 63 亿美元的加密货币盗窃案到底有多大？是谁干的？投资安全吗？
具有讽刺意味的是，朝鲜的互联网受到严格限制，普通民众无法使用。然而，数学和科学在学校里受到推崇，在大学里，一些最优秀的学生被招募到黑客组织中，例如在国家侦察总局间谍机构的支持下运作的拉撒路。
黑客攻击与强大的国家密切相关。 2014 年 12 月，令索尼影业尴尬的是，电影明星詹妮弗·劳伦斯和艾米·亚当斯的片酬低于《美国骗局》中的男演员。这是好莱坞工作室因黑客攻击而泄露的数千封令人尴尬的电子邮件之一。
朝鲜拉撒路集团发动这次袭击是因为索尼资助了一部描绘金正恩遇刺事件的塞斯·罗根喜剧《采访》。在爆料的混乱中，索尼试图取消这部电影，然后在因屈服于朝鲜压力而受到批评后，不得不掉头撤退，在网上和少数几家电影院上映。
